method:
Fresh independent static audit of every assigned current file in .work/round12/interface.json. Read complete file text in contiguous bounded chunks; finish partial files before advancing. Reread truncated or lost output ranges before counting them inspected. All 198 assigned files were fully read, including implementations, tests, styles, configuration, and documentation.
Trace gateway/core state, identity, authentication, authorization, operation receipts, unknown outcomes, recovery, websocket ownership, scheduling, process boundaries, and persistent-resource behavior through current implementation and tests.
Trace Web input, navigation, keyboard/accessibility semantics, asynchronous completion ownership, stale state, operation recovery, pagination, composer behavior, connection changes, and settings actions through current implementation and tests.
Only after a concrete source candidate, run the exact affected existing test file through the official targeted runner and bounded ignored jsdom probes rendering the current frozen component with mocked local API responses. No product code or tests changed.
Compare all 198 assigned files with their initial SHA-256 values separately from full-text review; compute the entire current source snapshot using node scripts/snapshot.mjs. Hash checks are integrity checks, not reading evidence.

findings.title: An expired pairing status query leaves the next pairing check disabled until the settings owner remounts
findings.evidence: The status handler sets the component-wide checking boolean true. Its finally clears checking only while scopeRef.current still matches the original pairScope. Expiry clears pairingId at line 50, changing the scope. A late status completion therefore cannot clear checking. Neither the owner-reset effect at line 48 nor creating a new pairing at line 62 resets or replaces that pending state. The next pairing renders its check button disabled by the retained checking=true at line 63.
reproduction: Render RemoteSettings with a stable epoch and connectionId; create pair-1 with an imminent expiry. Start its pairing/status read and hold the mocked response pending.
Allow pair-1 to expire, so the expiry message appears and pairingId is cleared.
Variant A: resolve the old read with claimed=false, then explicitly confirm and create pair-2. Variant B: create pair-2 first, then resolve the old read with claimed=true.
In both variants code-2 is visible but Check whether paired remains disabled. Clicking it dispatches no second pairing/status request.
Change connectionId to a new owner. The prior code is removed; explicitly creating code-3 produces an enabled check button. Its current claimed=true response hides code-3 normally.
findings.actual: Both bounded probes reproduced newStatusDisabled=true with pairingStarts=2 and statusReads=1. The late claimed=true response did not hide the new code, so the existing data-scope guard works, but its busy state is stranded. A new connection owner restored querying; a current successful claim still hid its code.
findings.expected: After expiry and explicit creation of a new pairing, its own check must be available and have independently owned pending state. A late old response must neither disable the new check nor clear a newer pending check nor apply the old claimed result.
findings.impact: The current mounted settings owner cannot query the new pairing status through this control; the user must remount the owner, for example by reopening settings or establishing a new connection. This is a functional UX dead end. The probes did not show an authorization bypass or stale claimed data applied to the new pairing.
findings.recommendation: Bind pending status-query state and cancellation to the current pairing owner/generation, and clear only the request that owns that state. Add focused regression coverage for expiry and replacement while an old status query is pending, including late success/failure, new-query overlap, disconnect/reconnect, and environment change.

validations.interpretation: The existing focused tests pass. They do not cover the reproduced pending-query/expiry race.

validations.error: The first ignored loader attempted to use a TypeScript public transpile API unavailable in the installed package (ScriptTarget was undefined). No component was rendered and no product assertion ran. This setup failure was retained; the ignored loader was changed to the installed Vite transformWithOxc export.

validations.interpretation: A successful probe execution confirms the defect assertion, not passing product behavior. All API calls were local mocked fetch responses; the only expiry wait was bounded to 1150 milliseconds.

The old claimed=true completion was delivered after creating the new pairing. The disabled check reproduced; changing connectionId remounted the owner and restored checking. API responses were local mocks.
All assigned current file hashes equal the hashes captured before reading.

limitations: No full suite or release claim. Full-suite validation remains a later gate subject to the repository audit prerequisites.
No Linux/SSH execution, online changes, live deployment, real provider calls, or personal credentials. These later validation boundaries were not run and are not represented as passed.

The jsdom probes validate component state and local request dispatch with synthetic data. They do not verify browser rendering, actual native pairing, or provider behavior. Only the concretely reproduced pairing race is reported; related failure and environment-switch variations are suggested regression coverage, not claimed executed probes.

The assigned current web/VERIFICATION.md body contains historical summaries. Its current body was read as assigned documentation; linked historical audit/fix reports were not opened and no prior issue list was used.
Parent, sibling, and old-project code, tests, assets, builds, and Git history were not read.

No frozen source, tests, feature-evidence, or documentation were edited. The official targeted runner wrote its own ignored .work/test-results artifacts; auditor-created probes and progress reside under ignored .work/round12.
Complete means all assigned files were fully audited. This report contains one confirmed finding and does not assert a clean round or approval to run subsequent release gates.
